description:
Some missions go silent. Their stories don’t. 🪐

THE LAST SIGNAL is a cinematic journey into the forgotten corners of space exploration, where abandoned machines become storytellers, lost signals become mysteries, and every discovery leaves a trace.

We’re here to bring their stories back to life. 🚀
summary: The Last Signal is a cinematic digital museum that tells the stories of NASA machines left on the Moon and Mars: InSight, Opportunity, and the Apollo 17 Lunar Roving Vehicle. A mysterious “signal detected” message pulls the visitor into a hidden space archive. There, an astronaut guide scans each machine to reveal its mission, its discoveries, how it ended, and its legacy. We built a 65-second cinematic film and a project website that hosts the film, a mission archive, a short quiz, and NASA sources. The project addresses the challenge by turning scattered technical facts into an experience young people want to explore. It matters because these missions did not end when the machines went silent: their data still shapes our understanding of Mars and the Moon. Our next step is a VR experience that lets visitors walk through the museum and stand next to the machines.
details:
What it does: The Last Signal is a story-driven museum experience made of a film and a website. The film opens with a visitor entering the museum site and receiving a “Signal Detected” alert. An astronaut guide then walks through the archive and scans InSight (the Mars listener that studied marsquakes), Opportunity (designed for 90 Martian days, it explored for almost 15 Earth years and found evidence of ancient water), and the Apollo 17 rover (which carried astronauts farther across the lunar surface).

Benefits and impact: It makes real mission science easy and exciting for young space enthusiasts. We separate verified NASA facts from artistic recreations.

Tools: Canva (visual identity and exhibit screens), CapCut (editing, sound, voice-over), a website builder (project site), and AI generation tools for the museum scenes, NASA resources, and AI tools

Creativity: Instead of a fact sheet, we used a mystery. A signal invites the visitor in, and each machine tells its own story.

Factors we considered: accuracy (verified NASA sources), age-friendly language, and clear labeling of AI-generated scenes.

Future work: A VR experience where visitors walk through the archive, see each machine at real scale, scan it, and take the quiz inside VR.
